newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Threats against Indian Jesus in Argentine church.
newsitem.headline: Threats against Indian Jesus in Argentine church.

text.p: A cathedral in northern Argentina has had to remove a nativity scene in which the holy family were represented with the features of Andean Indians after protests from local society women and threats of arson.
The nativity scene presented a life-size baby Jesus, Mary and Joseph modelled in styrofoam with the same dark faces as many of the local inhabitants of the city of Salta.

But the Clarin newspaper reported that a group of 15 women from local wealthy families wrote to Catholic authorities demanding the scene be taken out of Salta Cathedral, where it was first shown in 1993. It was removed and installed in a shopping mall after anonymous telephoned threats of arson.
While most Argentines are of European descent, there are a significant number of native Indians, particularly in the country's sparsely populated and impoverished north.
